summary: Frontend-only navbar navigation test focused on user bug 'Menù button cannot be clicked'. Verified on desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844). Intro loader unmounts within 3s; window.__lenis exists; document.elementFromPoint at center of nav-menu returns the nav-menu <button> itself (no overlay). Clicking Menù smoothly scrolls to #menu (scrollY 0 -> 1681, section top ~72px which equals the -72px offset). Same works after pre-scrolling 800px (still reaches scrollY 1681, top 72). All other nav links (filosofia, galleria, delivery, contatti) also scroll to their sections with top ~72px. Mobile: hamburger opens dropdown, tapping nav-mobile-menu scrolls to #menu (0 -> 1992, top 72) and the dropdown closes (link no longer in DOM). User-reported bug is NOT reproducible in current build.
action_items: User-reported bug 'Menù not clickable' could NOT be reproduced. Menù click reliably scrolls to #menu on both desktop and mobile, from top and from mid-page. If user still experiences issue, ask for browser/device and any console errors (possibly a stale cached bundle on their client).
critical_code_review_comments: Lenis warning in console: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative/fixed/absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' Consider adding position:relative to the scroll container root to silence and ensure offset accuracy.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Navbar links + smooth scroll (lenis) are fully functional as of iteration 3. scrollToId in SmoothScroll.jsx computes y correctly and calls window.__lenis.scrollTo. Menù resolves to #menu with top ~72px post-scroll (matches the -72 navbar offset). Mobile dropdown auto-closes via setOpen(false) in go().
rca of the issue: No reproducible bug. scrollToId computes numeric offset (getBoundingClientRect().top + pageYOffset - 72) and delegates to window.__lenis.scrollTo, which works. IntroLoader is pointer-events-none and unmounts by ~2.2s so it does not intercept clicks. elementFromPoint at nav-menu center returns the button itself — no overlay covering it. Likely a client-side cache issue on the reporter's browser prior to the latest deploy.
